title: Closed-complement vanishing for proper pushforward of open extension
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$; all schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible [sk-def-localizing-closure], with the finite-subextension condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories and total derived pushpull [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and exact termwise open extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Let $r:W\to\overline Y$ be a morphism, $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $U=W\times_{\overline Y}Y$, and $j:U\hookrightarrow W$, $p:U\to Y$ the projections [def-pc-fibre-product; def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume $r$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $c:Z\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be the reduced closed complement of $i(Y)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then for every bounded constructible complex of finite Tor amplitude $A\in\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $$c^*Rr_*j_!A\simeq0\quad\text{in }D(Z_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda).$$ This is a statement about the target object alone, with no comparison morphism or localizing-closure conclusion.

proof.text: Put $T=W\times_{\overline Y}Z$, with projections $a:T\to W$ and $r_Z:T\to Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-proper-open-complement-square] to the given $r,i,c$. It provides the proper Cartesian square inside the standing scheme setting, identifies $a$ and $j$ as complementary closed and quasi-compact open immersions (without assuming $T$ reduced), and gives $a^*j_!A\simeq0$.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs.

proof.text: Set $K=j_!A$. Apply [lem-sfb-open-extension-zero-constructible-finite-tor] to $j$ and $A$: it gives $K\in\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$ and also bounded constructibility in the ring-object sense. Thus $K$ satisfies both constructibility conventions in the coefficient-specific base-change nodes.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs.

proof.text:
Suppose $\Lambda$ is a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$. Apply clause (2) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite] to $r:W\to\overline Y$, $g=c$, $g'=a$, and $p'=r_Z$. Properness and the standing scheme hypotheses hold by step 1, and $K=j_!A$ lies in $\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$ by step 2. It follows that
$$c^*Rr_*j_!A\simeq R(r_Z)_*a^*j_!A.$$
Both sides are objects of the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category on $Z$. For a finite discrete coefficient presentation, identify its continuous-map condensed ring with the sheafified constant ring by lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, applying the canonical ring equivalence that removes the extra universe lift.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs.

proof.text:
For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ use clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral] on the same square and $K=j_!A\in\Dbc(W,\mathcal O_E)$ from step 2. This also covers $\mathbf Z_\ell$ by taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, whose valuation ring is $\mathbf Z_\ell$. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the adopted proper-base-change theorems [nt-target-proetale-e] and [nt-target-proetale-qbar], again on that square and bounded constructible $K$. The case $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. These cases and step 3 exhaust the admissible list in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The algebraic-closure coefficient is throughout the finite-subextension condensed ring fixed in the statement. We obtain in every case
$$c^*Rr_*j_!A\simeq R(r_Z)_*a^*j_!A.$$
Only bounded constructible inputs to these theorems are used, with no assertion on a localizing closure. Realize the ground field inside the fixed algebraic closure by an algebraic embedding and the uniqueness of the extended p-adic norm. The same norm uniqueness identifies the unit ball and the universe-lifted integral coefficient ring. Postcomposition gives the corresponding condensed ring isomorphisms. Transport constant-model finite-Tor inputs by lem-sfb-condensed-coefficient-iso-constructible. Scalar restriction along the inverse coefficient isomorphism is an exact equivalence, commutes with derived pullback and pushforward, preserves bounded constructibility (using lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback on cohomology), and reflects zero objects; thus the coefficient-specific vanishing statements transport to the given Lambda.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation on bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs.

proof.text: Substitute $a^*j_!A\simeq0$ from step 1 into the isomorphism of step 3 or 4. The derived adjunction $r_Z^*\dashv R(r_Z)_*$ implies $R(r_Z)_*0\simeq0$: for every $B$, its adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(B,R(r_Z)_*0)$ with the singleton $\operatorname{Hom}(r_Z^*B,0)$, so $R(r_Z)_*0$ is terminal and hence isomorphic to the zero object. Thus $c^*Rr_*j_!A\simeq0$, as claimed.
